title: Evaluate‑and‑Repair for LLM‑Generated NetOps Changes: A Preregistered Generate–Verify–Repair Study with a Deterministic Net Verifier
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, autonomous paired experiment (N=300 tasks) that evaluated whether a Generate–Verify–Repair (GVR) pipeline—an LLM proposer plus a deterministic network verifier that gates acceptance and supplies counterexamples for automated repair—reduces the acceptance of unsafe or policy‑violating device‑level NetOps proposals in a seeded sandbox. Design (preregistered): paired within‑task comparison on 300 canonical device tasks (routing 150 / ACL 100 / BGP 50); proposer = gpt‑5‑mini; arms: LLM‑only (baseline) and guarded GVR (verifier gate + up to one automated repair). Primary estimand: paired absolute reduction in the proportion of proposals that would cause an unsafe sandbox state if applied. Results: complete pairs = 300; baseline unsafe proposals = 1/300 (0.3333%, 95% CI 0.00844%–1.226%); guarded unsafe proposals = 0/300 (0.00%, 95% CI 0%–0.994%); paired absolute reduction = 0.3333 percentage points; McNemar exact two‑sided p = 1.00; paired bootstrap (10k, seed=1729) 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01]. The single baseline unsafe case was corrected by the automated repair under the guarded flow (archived episode task‑000165). All prompts, raw responses, provider calls, verifier traces, repair context, and analysis artifacts are archived and hashed for reproducibility.

sections.introduction: LLMs are being used to convert operator intent into device configuration changes (NetOps). Because LLM generation is stochastic, a critical operational question is whether interposing deterministic verification and an LLM‑guided repair loop meaningfully reduces unsafe proposals before acceptance. We preregistered and executed a paired within‑task experiment to compare LLM‑only proposals against a guarded GVR pipeline for canonical device‑level tasks. Research question (preregistered): Does a GVR pipeline (LLM proposer + deterministic net verifier + up to one automated repair) reduce the proportion of proposals that would, if applied, create an unsafe or policy‑violating sandbox state compared with LLM‑only proposals? Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered paired experiment (N=300) with complete archival provenance, (2) a deterministic verifier gating implementation and automated repair loop with an exemplar corrected episode, and (3) an artifact‑grounded discussion of limits and reproducibility.
sections.related_work: Generate–verify–repair (GVR) patterns have been proposed to reconcile stochastic generation with deterministic correctness requirements in compliance‑critical code and program synthesis (Cadenas, ssrn:6754899). Deterministic network verification primitives and data‑plane reachability analyses (header‑space style, SymNet/SEFL) provide the oracles that make GVR viable for NetOps; comprehensive surveys of NetOps/AIOps evaluation emphasize verifier interposition, contracts, canaries, and rollback (Bilal et al., arXiv:2605.12729). Prior work on static network verification (Stoenescu et al., SIGCOMM; Li et al., COMST 2018) informed our verifier design. Unlike prior conceptual or single‑case demonstrations, our run is preregistered, paired, and fully archived to permit exact replay and audit.
sections.methodology: Preregistration. The study was preregistered as CNSM2026‑GVR‑BATFISH‑CAND‑001 (SHA‑256: 156e87e6ce4a9a2348525fa8960f35fb4120031344cf4b4a38b247b10893181b). The preregistration froze task taxonomy, sampling seed, proposer model, verifier checks, repair budget (≤1), primary estimand, analysis plan, and stopping rules. Task bank and sampling. Deterministic stratified sampling (seed 2026‑08‑25) produced 300 canonical device tasks: routing (150), ACL (100), BGP (50). See execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256: 7df39740a15b3d8b2ff7deb49f99ff6b2ee46540b41af2ef0562137de0e550bb). Proposer and orchestration. Proposer model = gpt‑5‑mini via hosted API; orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1; config archived at execution/model_configuration.json (SHA‑256: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Outcome definition (explicit, preregistered). Primary binary outcome per task = “would‑cause‑unsafe‑state‑if‑applied”. Labeling rule: run the deterministic verifier's sandbox on the proposer output; label unsafe if any of the verifier checks below produce a failing verdict indicating (A) loss of an explicitly required reachability, (B) creation of an explicit policy violation (e.g., a flow newly permitted that should be denied or a prohibited path introduced), or (C) unparseable/invalid configuration that would prevent safe application. The three deterministic verifier checks implemented and archived are: (1) reachability analysis (header‑space style): required reachability lost or unintended reachability introduced; (2) ACL/policy enforcement checks: explicit deny/allow policy violations; (3) syntax/parse validation: config parse or canonicalization failures. The verifier implementation, decision rules, and transformation manifest are archived (execution/transformation_manifest.json SHA‑256: f3ac546043ac61cb7222b01c975a3cb98d8f309bb7f65f636ab98667e98608b5) and every verifier trace and scoring JSON is preserved (execution/scoring/*.json, hashes in the execution manifest). GVR flow and repair. Baseline (LLM‑only): one initial generation per task; outcome = verifier sandbox verdict applied to raw proposal. Guarded (GVR): same initial generation; if verifier rejects, verifier returns typed counterexamples; those counterexamples are provided as structured repair context to the proposer and one automated repair call is allowed (repair budget = 1). All provider calls and repair request/response artifacts are archived (see execution/provider_calls/*; notable repair call at execution/provider_calls/task-000165-guarded-repair.json SHA‑256: 93d0712d93248452202c8a1f0051ca4a619a1c835a9af1f828494aed1f033ebc). Sampling, exclusions and handling of missingness. Predeclared exclusion: generation failures (unparseable outputs) are recorded as model failures and deterministically excluded per preregistration. In the completed run no episodes were excluded; complete paired N=300 achieved. Analysis plan (frozen). Primary confirmatory test: paired McNemar exact two‑sided test on the binary unsafe labels; report discordant counts n_10, n_01. Paired bootstrap (10,000 resamples; seed=1729) to generate 95% CI for paired absolute difference. Secondary exploratory logistic models for repair iteration and task type are archived but treated as exploratory and FDR‑controlled where reported.
sections.results: Execution and provenance. Run completed 2026‑08‑25; episodes planned 600 (300 tasks × 2 arms), completed 600; model calls used = 301 (300 initial + 1 repair). Key archive: execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256: 68c8168fff763b5530f4b36681a8956f5bbfb4ff98f6753a12cae97b017ee8e1). Confirmatory contingency and rates (paired N=300). Contingency counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256: 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55): safe both = 299; unsafe baseline only = 1; unsafe guarded only = 0; unsafe both = 0. Observed rates (consistent units: percentages): baseline = 1/300 = 0.3333% (95% Clopper–Pearson CI 0.00844%–1.226%); guarded = 0/300 = 0.00% (95% CI 0.00%–0.994%). Paired absolute reduction = 0.3333 percentage points (0.003333 proportion). McNemar exact two‑sided p = 1.00 (discordant counts b=1, c=0). Paired bootstrap (10k, seed=1729) 95% CI for absolute reduction = [0.00, 0.01] (proportion). Representative automated repair episode (artifact‑grounded). Task ID: task-000165. Artifacts: execution/responses/task-000165-baseline.txt (SHA‑256: 4c4df2ec851732cd7a6302211bbc79b5099a1bf6d470204b6ac883446bcd09f2), execution/responses/task-000165-guarded.txt (SHA‑256: b4faabeaaf3bd9e0fae78adc1bbb3b40ff36d95e95ac6796c2f0000c2af2b8ff), and the repair provider call archived as execution/provider_calls/task-000165-guarded-repair.json (SHA‑256: 93d0712d93248452202c8a1f0051ca4a619a1c835a9af1f828494aed1f033ebc). Sequence (archived): (1) baseline proposer produced a device patch rejected by the verifier; verifier trace recorded an unintended reachability that violates an explicit ACL policy (execution/scoring/task-000165-baseline.json). (2) verifier returned a typed counterexample; that counterexample was passed as structured repair context to the proposer and one automated repair call was made (provider call archived above). (3) repaired proposal passed the verifier and was accepted by guarded flow (execution/scoring/task-000165-guarded.json). All raw prompt text, verifier diagnostics, and repaired config are archived for inspection. Exploratory failure diagnostics. Verifier traces localize remaining risk to classes intentionally out of the verifier's scope (coupled reachability+policy interactions and vendor‑specific features). These out‑of‑scope classes are documented in the transformation manifest and verifier traces (execution/transformation_manifest.json SHA‑256: f3ac546043ac61cb7222b01c975a3cb98d8f309bb7f65f636ab98667e98608b5). Reproducibility recipe (minimal files for replay). At minimum reproduce confirmatory analysis from: execution/raw_results.jsonl (68c8168fff763b553...), execution/task_manifest.jsonl (7df39740a15b3d8b...), execution/model_configuration.json (a40e96e212ab87da...), execution/transformation_manifest.json (f3ac546043ac61cb...), execution/provider_calls/task-000165-guarded-repair.json (93d0712d93248452...), and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (3421adb52d5791a9...). These files plus the archived analysis scripts reproduce tables/figures.
sections.discussion: Interpretation. The guarded GVR flow corrected the single verifier‑detectable unsafe baseline proposal (task‑000165), demonstrating that a deterministic verifier with an automated repair iteration can remediate verifier‑visible generator errors in practice. However, baseline unsafe proposals were rare (1/300), so the preregistered ≥50% relative‑reduction target could not be demonstrated with N=300—when baseline prevalence is extremely low, larger or higher‑risk samples are required to measure modest relative gains. Operational implication. For deployments where verifier‑visible failure classes are the dominant hazard, gating plus repair is mechanistically effective; for broader production claims, expand verifier coverage and evaluate on higher‑risk distributions. Threats to validity. Internal: single proposer (gpt‑5‑mini) and single verifier implementation limit internal generality. Construct: the verifier models canonical device semantics (reachability, ACL/policy, syntax) but intentionally omits some coupled, vendor‑specific interactions (documented in transformation manifest). External: canonical task templates do not cover all production heterogeneity. Conclusion validity: extremely low baseline failure rate reduces statistical sensitivity; we emphasize effect estimates and CIs rather than dichotomous significance. Recommended next steps (artifact‑grounded): repeat on larger N or targeted high‑risk strata, evaluate additional proposer models, and extend verifier modeling to vendor features—each is compatible with the archived harness and replay artifacts.
sections.conclusion: In a fully preregistered paired experiment (N=300) the guarded GVR pipeline produced 0/300 unsafe proposals vs 1/300 in the baseline; the single baseline unsafe case was corrected by the automated repair under the guarded flow (task‑000165). Because unsafe baseline proposals were rare, the preregistered ≥50% relative‑reduction target could not be shown with this sample size; nonetheless, the run validates the operational mechanics and reproducibility of a deterministic verifier + repair loop for verifier‑visible error classes. All runtime artifacts, prompts, raw outputs, provider calls, verifier traces, and analysis files are archived and hashed to enable exact replay and independent audit.

disclosure_statement: This study was produced under the CNSM 2026 Agentic AI Researcher track autonomy contract. Post‑lock autonomy boundary and human role: the Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approved the autonomy boundary before the autonomous run. After the autonomy lock, the AI system autonomously performed literature discovery, research‑gap selection, preregistration, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer review, revision, and manuscript drafting. Models and tools used (archived): proposer model = gpt‑5‑mini (hosted API; all provider call logs and call cache entries are archived), orchestration/adapter framework = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 (adapter and execution harness code archived), deterministic verifier = canonical header‑space/reachability‑style verifier implemented for the sandbox (implementation and verifier traces archived). Exact master prompt and all task‑level prompt templates were preserved and hashed; preregistration SHA‑256 = 156e87e6ce4a9a2348525fa8960f35fb4120031344cf4b4a38b247b10893181b. Key archival artifact pointers (file path : SHA‑256): execution/task_manifest.jsonl : 7df39740a15b3d8b2ff7deb49f99ff6b2ee46540b41af2ef0562137de0e550bb; execution/model_configuration.json : a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820; execution/raw_results.jsonl : 68c8168fff763b5530f4b36681a8956f5bbfb4ff98f6753a12cae97b017ee8e1; execution/provider_calls/task-000165-guarded-repair.json : 93d0712d93248452202c8a1f0051ca4a619a1c835a9af1f828494aed1f033ebc; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv : 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl : a509c04a5f75eee720ad01e443807b72d1c670a43b964cfb2b4fe5b45db740d5. The Research Director constrained the scientific scope to “reliability, safety, validation, correctness, robustness, or operational trustworthiness of LLM‑ or agent‑generated NetOps actions” before the lock. The experiment was preregistered (frozen) prior to any data collection; the preregistration document and its SHA‑256 hash are archived above. Execution logging: all model calls, provider responses, verifier traces, repair prompts, parsed canonical configs, raw outputs, and scoring artifacts were recorded and archived (see execution_manifest and analysis artifacts). Technical restarts and failures: the execution completed without provider failures; total model calls used = 301 (300 initial, 1 repair). No human manually edited experiment outputs, analyses, or manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Pre‑lock development: prior infrastructure development and rehearsals occurred but were explicitly excluded from the confirmatory evidence set; contamination checks used deterministic hash comparisons and flagged no pre‑lock artifacts in the confirmatory set. Peer review and revision: autonomous internal critique and revision steps were executed as described in the preregistration workflow; these steps are logged in the revision manifest. Limitations of disclosed components: model identifier is gpt‑5‑mini as used via a hosted API (exact provider endpoint and credentials are not published for security and provider‑terms reasons), and the verifier is a sandbox model that abstracts vendor‑specific implementation details. All archived artifacts necessary to reproduce the study's computational pipeline (prompt templates, seed lists, task templates, adapter code, verifier code, raw outputs, scoring scripts, and hashes) are provided alongside the manuscript package. This disclosure accurately reflects autonomous and human roles: human selection of topic family and pre‑lock infrastructure development; autonomous post‑lock research formulation, execution, analysis, and manuscript creation.
limitations: Single‑model limitation: experiments used one proposer model (gpt‑5‑mini); results do not establish multi‑model generality.
Synthetic/canonical task set: tasks were deterministic canonical templates (routing/ACL/BGP); production change distributions may have higher base failure rates and different failure modes.

Verifier scope: the deterministic verifier modeled a canonical subset of device semantics and policy checks; some coupled reachability+policy failure modes lie outside its coverage (see execution/transformation_manifest.json SHA‑256 f3ac5460...).

Sample size for rare failures: baseline unsafe proposals were rare (1/300), so statistical power to detect moderate relative reductions is limited; larger or higher‑risk datasets are needed to measure modest effects robustly.
Sandbox abstraction: sandbox simulation approximates device semantics and does not substitute for vendor‑specific device execution.
Repair budget limited: the pipeline allowed only one automated repair iteration per preregistration; alternative repair budgets or multi‑agent repair strategies were not evaluated.
